title: First-order convergence to local minimax optima
formal:
Consider sequential minimax optimization \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^p}\max_{y\in\mathbb R^q} f(x,y)\), with \(p,q\ge1\), \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^{p+q},\mathbb R)\), and a supplied constant \(L>0\) satisfying
\[\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le L\|z-w\|_2\qquad\text{for all }z,w\in\mathbb R^{p+q}.\]
Does there exist one uniform deterministic first-order oracle method, in the model below, that produces iterates \(z_k=(x_k,y_k)\) from every initial point and has both of these properties for every such \(p,q,f,L\)?

First, for Lebesgue-almost every initial point \(z_0\), whenever the complete sequence \((z_k)_{k\ge0}\) converges to a finite point \(z^*\), that point is a local minimax point in the neighborhood definition below. Second, every strict local minimax point has an open neighborhood of initial points from which the method converges to that point. The second requirement excludes a method that satisfies the first merely by never converging.
why: Sequential adversarial optimization needs the minimization and maximization roles to be respected at the limiting solution. Reaching a stationary point alone can select the wrong kind of equilibrium. A first-order selection theorem that remains valid with degeneracy would clarify what gradient information can guarantee beyond the curvature-restricted cases already analyzed.
status_note: Reviewed on 16 September 2026. The primary 2023 source poses a broad open direction; the complete oracle and convergence quantifiers on this card are an explicitly chosen benchmark variant. The inspected 2024 results retain derivative, matrix, spectral or global-structure hypotheses, and the August 2026 constrained result concerns approximate stationarity under a KL assumption. Bounded searches did not establish a validated solution of both guarantees here. A further OpenReview submission advertises calmness-based selection in indexed passages, but its full current text and status were inaccessible in this pass and have not been verified. The card remains uncertain and active; the formulation is complete, while the dated literature check is expressly limited.

progress.text: Jin, Netrapalli and Jordan formalize local minimax optimality for sequential games and connect two-timescale gradient dynamics with it subject to degeneracy qualifications.
The COLT open-problem contribution asks for first-order convergence to genuine local minimax optima and explains the remaining gap beyond necessary derivative conditions.
The current ICLR extragradient version extends the covered non-strict cases, while retaining matrix and spectral assumptions.
The ICML double-step alternating method improves local stability, including an increasing-timescale analysis under additional assumptions.
Lu–Wang establish constrained approximate-stationarity guarantees under a local KL assumption; this does not certify the selected unrestricted limit property.

category_assignment.reason: The target is the convergence behavior of a first-order minimax optimization method, independent of a hypothesis-learning problem.

importance.reason: Whether first-order information can select the correct local optima of sequential nonconvex–nonconcave games is a basic convergence question for adversarial optimization. Its scope is local solution selection rather than unrestricted efficient global optimization.
importance.basis: Individual review of the COLT 2023 open problem, the original local-optimality definition and subsequent convergence results; editorial significance assessment.

sentences: In sequential minimax optimization, one player minimizes a smooth function of x while a second player maximizes it in y.
A local minimax point respects this order using shrinking neighborhoods whose radii may differ for the two players.
The selected variant asks for one deterministic method with exact function-value and gradient queries whose finite limits are local minimax points for almost every initialization.
The same method must converge locally to every strict local minimax point, so avoiding convergence everywhere is not a valid answer.
Existing convergence theorems retain extra hypotheses or weaker derivative-based targets, and the exact variant and limits of the current source review are explicitly recorded.

definitions:
The order of play is fixed: \(x\) is the minimization variable and \(y\) is the maximization variable. All norms are Euclidean. A point \(z^*=(x^*,y^*)\) is a local minimax point if there exist \(\delta_0>0\) and a function \(h:(0,\delta_0]\to[0,\infty)\), with \(\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}h(\delta)=0\), such that for every \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\) and all \(x,y\) with \(\|x-x^*\|_2\le\delta\) and \(\|y-y^*\|_2\le\delta\),
\[f(x^*,y)\le f(x^*,y^*)\le
 \max_{\|y'-y^*\|_2\le h(\delta)} f(x,y').\]
The closed maximization ball is nonempty and compact, so the maximum exists. The radius function may depend on \(f,z^*\). There is no additional bound on \(h(\delta)/\delta\), no restriction to a Hessian range, and no assumption of concavity in \(y\). In particular, local minimax does not mean a simultaneous local Nash equilibrium or a global minimax solution.

A stationary point satisfies \(\nabla f(z^*)=0\). Define its Hessian blocks
\[A=\nabla^2_{xx}f(z^*)\in\mathbb R^{p\times p},\quad
 B=\nabla^2_{yy}f(z^*)\in\mathbb R^{q\times q},\quad
 C=\nabla^2_{xy}f(z^*)\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}.\]
A strict local minimax point here means a stationary point satisfying
\[B\prec0,\qquad A-CB^{-1}C^{\mathsf T}\succ0.\]
For a symmetric matrix, positive definiteness means that its quadratic form is positive on every nonzero vector; negative definiteness is defined with a negative sign. These sufficient conditions imply the neighborhood definition above. They define the points at which attraction is required, not a promise on every stationary point or every local minimax point of the input. Degenerate and non-strict points remain subject to the first, limit-selection requirement.

A first-order oracle queried at \(z\in\mathbb R^{p+q}\) returns the exact pair \((f(z),\nabla f(z))\). The function is available only through this oracle, not through its formula, a Hessian oracle, a maximization oracle or a best-response oracle. A method is one fixed finite real-arithmetic program supplied with \(p,q,L,z_0\), initialized with empty history and fixed rational constants. It uses scalar addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by nonzero numbers, exact comparisons, branching, copying, and integer loop/address operations. Real registers cannot be inspected digit by digit. Oracle calls may be adaptive, at points computed from the supplied data and earlier replies. Finite differences or other numerical quantities computed from finitely many permitted replies are allowed; direct derivative queries above first order are not.

The program may retain finite history and use iteration-dependent or adaptively chosen parameters. On every permitted input and after every finite iteration count it must finish the finite work needed to produce the next iterate, using finitely many elementary operations, stored values and oracle calls. No infinite inner loop, exact limit operation, uncharged auxiliary oracle, function-dependent advice or external randomization is allowed. Auxiliary storage is finite at each finite stage but need not have a fixed bound over the infinite run. This is an asymptotic convergence question: no polynomial iteration bound, oracle-complexity rate or bit-complexity bound is requested. The real oracle and exact arithmetic are part of the model, not claims about finite-precision implementation.

For precision, let \(z_k^{f,L}(u)\) be the sequence produced from initial point \(u\), with dimensions understood and \(z_0^{f,L}(u)=u\). The first guarantee means that, for each \(p,q,f,L\), there exists a set \(E_{f,L}\subseteq\mathbb R^{p+q}\) of Lebesgue outer measure zero such that
\[\forall u\notin E_{f,L}\ \forall z^*,\quad
 \lim_{k\to\infty}z_k^{f,L}(u)=z^*
 \ \Longrightarrow\ z^*\text{ is a local minimax point of }f.\]
The one exceptional set must cover all possible bad limits, not a separate uncountable union of exceptions for individual points. Equivalently, the same implication must hold almost surely for every initialization distribution with a density with respect to Lebesgue measure. The algorithm itself is deterministic.

The second guarantee means that for every strict local minimax point \(z^*\), there exists \(r>0\), depending on \(f,L,z^*\), such that
\[\forall u\in\mathbb R^{p+q},\quad
 \|u-z^*\|_2<r\ \Longrightarrow\ \lim_{k\to\infty}z_k^{f,L}(u)=z^*.\]
Every start uses the same program initialization; no target point or attracting radius is supplied to it. The requirements permit divergent or nonconvergent runs outside these local basins. They concern limits of the full sequence, not every subsequential accumulation point, and do not require global convergence or attraction to every non-strict local minimax point.
answer_criterion:
Give a complete, mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the existence of a method meeting both guarantees, or of its logical negation. A positive proof must specify one finite oracle program, establish that it produces every next iterate after finite work, prove the common measure-zero exception statement for every permitted objective and every valid supplied \(L\), and prove local attraction at every point satisfying the strict Hessian conditions.

A negative proof must exclude every method in this specified oracle model from satisfying the conjunction. Counterexamples only to gradient descent-ascent, extragradient or another named update do not exclude every method. A method that never converges, convergence only to stationary points or second-order necessary-condition points, local linear stability without the stated limit guarantees, or a theorem assuming additional curvature or neighborhood-radius restrictions does not meet this target. No finite iteration rate is demanded, and the benchmark's numerical tolerance does not replace exact convergence or exact local minimaxity.

source_formulation.text: Editorial choice of a concrete benchmark variant, as authorized for source questions that leave the target unspecified. The COLT 2023 contribution poses a broad first-order convergence question and discusses both local stability and alternative notions of local optimality; it does not specify one complete oracle model or every convergence quantifier. This card keeps its original Jin–Netrapalli–Jordan neighborhood definition, includes degenerate objectives, and fixes deterministic exact first-order oracle access. The chosen target is almost-everywhere correctness of finite limits, together with local attraction at every strict local minimax point to prevent vacuous nonconvergence. This is stronger than a statement only about linearly stable fixed points and is not asserted to be a verbatim or proved-equivalent formulation of the source title. Global convergence, attraction to all non-strict points, fixed-step restrictions, and a different restricted-minimax definition are not part of this selected variant.

context_blocks.text: Both \(f(x,y)=x^2-y^2\) and \(g(x,y)=-x^2+y^2\) have zero gradient at the origin. For the prescribed minimization in \(x\) and maximization in \(y\), the first has a strict local minimax point there, while the second fails even the required local maximization in \(y\). Thus stationarity does not identify the intended local solution.

The local minimax definition allows the maximizing player’s response neighborhood to shrink at a different rate from the minimizing player’s neighborhood. It describes the sequential order of play. Requiring the minimizing player to keep the maximizer’s action fixed instead gives the stronger local Nash notion; reversing the players gives a different local optimization question.

The original convergence literature distinguishes sufficient strict curvature conditions from necessary second-order conditions. With degeneracy, satisfying the latter need not certify a local minimax point. A guarantee stated only for strict linearly unstable points also does not automatically exclude convergence to every other undesirable stationary point.

The ICLR 2024 two-timescale extragradient paper extends analysis beyond an invertible maximizing-player Hessian. Its theorems still retain conditions on the restricted Schur complement, the full saddle-gradient Jacobian or spectral thresholds. Its stable points are characterized using necessary second-order conditions in the relevant regimes; this is not the unrestricted true-minimax limit guarantee selected here.

The ICML 2024 double-step alternating extragradient work improves local stability for further non-strict cases and studies increasing timescale separation. Its local results retain nondegeneracy conditions on specified Hessian-derived matrices; the increasing-timescale stability theorem additionally assumes a third derivative. The paper’s separate global-convergence result assumes star-convex–star-concave structure. Those hypotheses are absent from this card’s objective class.

Follow-the-Ridge gives a related local fixed-point theorem using second-order information and an invertible maximizing-player Hessian. Its distinction between strict linear stability and weak spectral stability also matters. This is a useful comparison with the first-order question, but its Hessian-assisted theorem is not a solution for every objective in the model here.

Lu and Wang’s August 2026 constrained minimax paper proves complexity bounds for approximate stationary points under a local Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz condition on a lifted inner problem. That condition restricts the relation between objective residuals and generalized gradients. The assumptions and approximate-stationarity target differ from exact local-minimax limit selection for arbitrary smooth objectives.

The probability qualifier concerns the initial point. It allows, for example, an exceptional initialization exactly at an undesirable stationary point when such starts form a null set. The local-attraction condition supplies a positive guarantee near strict solutions. No convergence assertion is being made for every trajectory of a nonconvex–nonconcave game.
